items.title: Section 9D and the limits of undoing MADA: Can Parliament fetter the States' Entry 49 power?
items.summary: The latest amendment to the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 ( MMDR Act), which received the assent of the President on August 17, has brought about significant changes. Some are viewed as being in accord with the Supreme Court's decision in Mineral Area Development Authority v. Steel Authority of India (2024) (the MADA case - a nine-judge bench decision), but some that could very well be viewed as a direct challenge to what the Court has held in this landmark case. The MADA case alters the position of law that had held the field since 1990, when a seven-judge bench of the Supreme Court, in India Cement Ltd v. State of Tamil Nadu (1990) , held that the imposition of royalty by a State under Section 9 of the MMDR Act was really a levy of a tax relatable to Entry 50 in the State List, regulated by Parliament, tracing its power to Entry 54 in the Union List. It further held that the field of taxation with respect to Entry 50 stood occupied by virtue of Section 9 and that, as such, the State could not levy a cess on royalty. A cess, being a further tax, was not permitted by Section 9. The issue at the heart of the controversy today is: can Parliament, through the present amendment, fetter the State's competence to levy tax on mineral-bearing lands by providing restrictions through the newly inserted Section 9D ? The provision is not notified and no conditions have been prescribed under it by the Central government so far. It is necessary first to understand what Section 9D actually does to the State's power over mineral-bearing land. It has both a prospective and a retrospective operation. Prospectively, it provides that the State shall not tax mineral-bearing land at all, whether the tax is measured by the quantity of mineral, its value, or the royalty payable, except in accordance with such conditions as the Central government may prescribe. Since no such conditions have been prescribed, the State's power to tax stands, for the present, wholly suspended. The retrospective operation goes further. Any tax that a State had levied but had not collected before the amendment came into force is to be treated as invalid at all material times - from inception, notwithstanding any judgment, decree or order of any court. What a State had already collected is saved. items.title: Courts must protect poor to preserve India's socialist goal in Constitution: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently stressed that courts must ensure the protection of rights of weaker sections of the society to preserve the ‘socialist’ structure of India envisaged in the preamble of the Constitution.[ Union of India and Ors Vs Mithai Lal and Ors ]. The Division Bench of Justice C Hari Shankar and Justice Om Prakash Shukla made these observations in a matter concerning regularisation of the vendors engaged by Indian Railways. “It is time that Courts protected the interests of the weaker sections of the society and persons drawing paltry wages, so as to ensure that the socialist structure of our democracy – which is a preambular goal – remains intact,” the Court said in a judgement delivered on September 8. The petitioner-vendors had initially been engaged on a commission basis by the Railways. After years of service, they moved the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) claiming regularisation of their services in Railways. In a 2016 order, the CAT directed Railways to regularise the services of the vendors within 90 days along with allowances and cost of litigation. It also observed that the vendors were very poor people who had spent a considerable amount of money in running from pillar to post to get their dues. The Central government sought review of the order, which was dismissed. Thereafter, it moved the High Court against the CAT order. The Railways submitted that they absorbed some of the eligible bearers/ vendors into regular service in Group-D posts. The Court said the Railways could not have resorted to any process of screening to eliminate some or even any of them from regularisation. It also said that the Railways was unable to substantiate that several of the respondents (those who approached CAT) had been absorbed as Group-D employees. “To say the least, this is very disturbing. One would expect the Railways to display candour both before the Tribunal as well as before this Court,” it said. The Court added that for decades, no substantial progress took place with respect to the absorption or regularisation of vendors and bearers in the Railways. “it is a matter of deep regret that low paid Group-D employees, working as bearers and vendors, are having to litigate for decades in order to secure their just entitlements, despite the directions issued by the Supreme Court on more than one occasion,” it said. items.title: Plea before Kerala High Court seeks disqualification of MLA Mani C Kappan after cheque bounce conviction
items.summary: A petition has been filed before the Kerala High Court seeking the disqualification of Member of Legislative Assembly (MLA) Mani C Kappan following his conviction earlier this month in a cheque dishonour case. [ Dinesh Menon v. State of Kerala & Ors. ] On September 1, a Mumbai court convicted Pala MLA Kappan in four cases under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, and sentenced him to a cumulative three and a half years of simple imprisonment. He was also ordered to pay ₹5.30 crores as compensation to the complainant in all four cases, businessman Dinesh Menon. The petition seeking Kappan's disqualification was filed before the High Court by Menon himself. In his petition, Menon has submitted that the order of the Mumbai court does not state that the sentences are to run concurrently. He has argued that as per legal precedents, upon conviction and impostition of sentence of over two years, sitting MLAs are to be immediately disqualified. However, Kappan continues to hold his position and no formal notification has been issued declaring his seat vacant. Menon has stated that he has already submitted a formal representation to the Speaker of the State Legislative Assembly seeking Kappan's disqualification. However, since no action has yet been taken, Menon says he has been constrained to move the High Court with the present petition seeking orders disqualifying the United Democratic Front (UDF) legislator. Menon is being represented by advocates V Sethunath, Thomas Abraham, Sreeganesh U, and Shamnas S.

items.title: Delhi High Court slams Punjab & Sind Bank for denying reward to manager who foiled robbery in 1998
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently directed the Punjab & Sind Bank to pay an amount of ₹50,000, along with an annual interest of 12 percent, to a manager who had foiled a robbery attempt at its Najafgarh Branch in 1998 [ Surjit Singh Vs Punjab & Sind Bank] . Justice Neena Bansal Krishna also awarded litigation costs of ₹2 lakh to the manager, Surjit Singh, while taking exception to the management’s conduct of making him suffer litigation for 28 years over compensation for his bravery. The Court said that instead of the bank and the government itself rewarding Singh in accordance with the relevant guidelines, they added insult to injury by asserting that his act was not covered by the guidelines. "Such conduct is not becoming of the Bank, which itself, in fact, should have rewarded and acknowledged the Petitioner for his exemplary conduct, rather than driving him to seek reward to which he was entitled. It has taken him since 28 years to get the validation of his act," the Court said. The Court added that the question was not of money but of the honour, which should have come to him on its own without litigation. Justice Neena Bansal Krishna The Court observed that the robbery incident was straight out of fiction. One winter afternoon in December 1998, five armed robbers stormed into the bank with automatic weapons. The armed security guards surrendered their weapons and the cashier complied with the robbers’ threats for cash. Singh, despite being surrounded by the robbers and a revolver placed on his temple, reached out and pressed the emergency alarm button. This caused the panicked robbers to run towards the door. Singh blocked their way, causing the bag containing stolen cash to fall. Ultimately, the robbers were able to steal only ₹75,000 out of the ₹40 lakh they had initially seized. After the incident, Singh’s bravery in foiling the robbery attempt was publicly lauded in the media by the bank management. The General Manager of the bank recommended Singh for an award. As per a Government of India (GoI) circular issued in 1991, bank employees who actively resist bank robberies may be granted compensation of up to ₹50,000 and an out-of-turn promotion. Accordingly, Singh claimed the benefits of this circular by writing several letters to the bank management. However, the bank rejected his claim, stating that as a bank manager, Singh was only carrying out his duty and his actions cannot be termed as bravery. He then moved the Court in 2005. items.title: Teacher hitting girl students on back, waist without sexual intent not offence under POCSO Act: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court has recently quashed a case under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act) against a school teacher accused of hitting minor girl students on their back and waist during class [Bhaskar Paul v. State of West Bengal]. In an order passed on September 8, a bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar held that the students’ statements did not indicate that the teacher had touched them with sexual intent, which is necessary to constitute sexual assault under the POCSO Act. The Court acknowledged that the teacher’s use of corporal punishment was inappropriate and that he should have been more sensitive while dealing with girl students. However, it said that such conduct alone could not justify prosecuting him for aggravated sexual assault under the POCSO Act. The Bench also highlighted the serious and irreversible damage that a POCSO prosecution could cause to a teacher’s life and career even if he were to be eventually acquitted. “ For a teacher serving in a girls’ school or a school which is co-educational, such an allegation or trial virtually amounts to condemning him, not only for his entire service career as a teacher but for his life as well. He has a family also. Therefore, to accuse a teacher of committing sexual assault on girl students, would be like a death knell for such a teacher. Ultimate acquittal would not redeem the appellant as it would be wholly inadequate to undo all the pervasive damage already suffered by him due to the severity of the criminal trial under the POCSO Act. While the appellant certainly needs to sensitize himself while dealing with students of tender age, particularly girl students, it cannot be a ground for prosecuting him under the stringent provisions of the POCSO Act, ” the Court said. items.summary: The Delhi High Court has reduced the sentence of a man convicted of rape and kidnapping a 14-year-old girl after noting that she had his name tattooed on her chest and had voluntarily travelled with him to Manali. [Vakul Kapoor Vs State] Justice Vimal Kumar Yadav said the circumstances indicated that the two were in an “amorous relationship”, though the girl’s age meant that the relationship could not legally be recognised. Therefore, the Court held that the nearly two years and four months already undergone by the man in custody would be sufficient punishment. The Court particularly referred to the tattoos and the girl’s conduct. “ Deep down somewhere, she must also be looking for answers and explanation for the tattoos and travel to Manali, etc, ” the Court observed. items.summary: The Himachal Pradesh High Court recently held that a promise of marriage may not amount to the offence of deceitful sexual intercourse when both the accused and the victim are already married to other people and were aware of each other’s marital status [Vinod Kumar v State of Himachal Pradesh] . Justice Sandeep Sharma made the observation while granting bail to one Vinod Kumar, an astrologer, accused of sexually assaulting a 31-year-old woman on the alleged promise of marriage. In the order dated September 3, the Court noted that both the accused and the woman were married to other people and neither had divorced their respective spouses. It therefore found that there was prima facie no question of a promise to marry. "There was no question of promise to marry, especially when factum of marriage of the petitioner as well victim/prosecutrix was in the know of the victim/prosecutrix as well as bail petitioner. Once victim/prosecutrix as well as petitioner had not taken divorce from their respective spouses, they otherwise could not have solemnize marriage," held the Court. She alleged that he had persuaded her to divorce her husband after examining her horoscope, which he claimed showed no prospects of a happy marriage. He had also allegedly told her that he had strained relations with his wife and would marry her after her divorce. items.summary: The Supreme Court on September 10 flagged several gaps in the FSSAI’s proposal for hexagon shaped warning labels on packaged foods high in sugar, salt and fat [ 3S And Our Health Society v. Union of India & Anr. ]. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran sought a timeline for introducing the labels and questioned the proposed two-phase rollout, particularly the plan to initially cover only products high in at least two of sugar, salt and fat rather than all products high in any one of these nutrients. The Bench gave the FSSAI 10 days to respond and posted the matter for further hearing on September 28. Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice Vinod Chandran The Court was hearing a public interest litigation (PIL) plea seeking the display of warning labels on packaged food items to indicate their salt, sugar and fat levels. During an earlier hearing, the Bench had criticised the FSSAI’s handling of the issue and questioned whether the regulator was bowing to corporate pressure instead of acting on a matter concerning public health, particularly the health of children. The FSSAI subsequently filed an affidavit dated August 28 proposing red-coloured hexagonal labels for products high in any two or more of added saturated fat, added sugar and salt. The proposed labels would state “HIGH FAT”, “HIGH SUGAR”, “HIGH SALT” and, where applicable, “HIGHLY SWEETENED BEVERAGE”. The font would be one point larger than the font used in the nutrition table on the back of the package. Bowing to corporate pressure? The second phase would cover products high in any one of the nutrients. The Court acknowledged that “significant progress” has been made since its previous order but said several aspects of the proposal remained unclear. It questioned the basis for dividing the rollout into two phases, noting that sugar, salt and saturated fat could each be harmful independently. It also sought a fixed timeline between the phases, warning that the second phase could otherwise be indefinitely postponed. items.summary: A Mumbai court has granted bail to Abhirup Ashim Paul, a student of the Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS), who was arrested for allegedly raising slogans supporting jailed activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam. [Abhirup Paul v. State of Maharashtra & Ors.] Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Dattatray Shankarrao Khedekar observed that Paul had already undergone custodial interrogation for sufficient period. Pertinently, the Court also said that there was no evidence linking him to any Maoist or any other banned organisation. “Prima facie except suspicion, there is no material to link the activities of the accused with mind set of maoist or against the nation or associating with banned organization against India,” the judge noted. The Court observed that having soft copies of the Maoist books and raising campus slogans in support of jailed activists did not amount to anti-national activity and an inference of being a Moaist cannot be drawn from the same. "Merely because of finding of pdf books (on Maoism), the inference of connection with the mind set of maoist can not be draw," the Court ruled. He determined that keeping Paul, a young offender, behind bars on mere suspicion would be unjust and detrimental to his career. The case stemmed from a first information report (FIR) filed on a complaint by the TISS Registrar over an unauthorised campus event. On October 12, 2025, students gathered at the institute to commemorate the death anniversary of the late professor GN Saibaba. During the gathering, the prosecution alleged that students raised slogans demanding the release of Khalid and Imam who are in jail in a case under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). After the sessions court rejected his anticipatory bail plea, Paul was arrested and taken into custody on August 7. Merely because of finding of pdf books (on Maoism), the inference of connection with the mind set of maoist can not be draw. The police alleged that Paul’s actions may be linked to a broader threat against the nation and were intended to create hatred in the community. However, the Magistrate rejected these suspicions. “Prima facie there is no incriminating material on record to justify involvement of the accused (Paul) against the nation,” the judge held. items.title: Supreme Court seeks response from Centre, States on plea seeking national welfare scheme for private school teachers
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday sought responses from the Union government and States on a plea seeking a comprehensive national welfare framework for private school teachers across the country [ Ligimol George v. Union of India & Ors. ]. A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta issued notice on the petition filed by Ligimol George, National Coordinator of the All India Teachers Federation. Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta The petitioner moved the Court contending that private school teachers form a substantial part of India's teaching workforce but do not have a dedicated national statutory mechanism for their welfare. Hence, a National Private School Teachers Welfare Board or a similar institutional mechanism to coordinate and monitor welfare measures across States should be established, it was submitted. According to the petition, existing laws such as the Employees' State Insurance Act, Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, Payment of Gratuity Act and the Code on Social Security, 2020 provide only limited or fragmented protection to private school teachers, depending on eligibility requirements and State-specific regulations. The petitioner relied on the UDISE+ 2023-24 data to highlight the scale of the issue. As per the same, 37,30,047 teachers are employed in recognised private unaided schools across India. According to the petition, many private school teachers work on contractual, temporary, ad hoc, fixed-pay or annually renewable appointments and retire without assured pension, adequate medical assistance, insurance, disability protection or other post-retirement benefits. The absence of uniform welfare protection results in unequal treatment of teachers performing substantially similar functions across States and institutions, it was contended. The petition was filed through advocate Deepak Prakash. items.title: Kerala High Court asks State to create 229 posts to address staff shortage in Consumer Commissions
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Wednesday asked the State government to take effective steps for the creation of 229 staff posts to augment the infrastructural development of Consumer fora in the State [Adv J Surya v State of Kerala & ors and connected case]. A bench of Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice Syam Kumar VM passed the order while considering a Public Interest Litigation petition filed by advocate J Surya and a connected petition filed by one CK Mithran concerning the functioning and infrastructure of State and district consumer commissions. " There is a need for the creation of 229 posts for the purpose of infrastructural development of the Consumer Dispute Redressal Commissions in all districts, including the State Commission, " the Court observed. It had earlier put in place an interim arrangement to address the shortage of staff in consumer commissions through its order dated August 5, 2026 and stated that the arrangement would continue until the proposed new posts were created. In that order, the Court had recorded the State's submission that for the time being, civil police officers already assigned to court duties in magistrate and sessions court could be given additional duty at consumer commissions across the State without creating additional posts. Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice Syam Kumar VM (Kerala HC) When the matter was heard on September 9, the Special Government Pleader informed the Court that the proposal for creating these posts was presently awaiting financial approval and the necessary financial sanction was expected to be granted in four weeks. Taking note of the submission, the Court posted the matter for further consideration on October 7, while asking the State to ensure that steps are taken towards creating the 229 posts by then. The Court also asked the State to file an affidavit detailing the progress made. " We hope that, by the adjourned date, effective steps shall have been taken for the creation of the posts, " the Court added. Advocates R Rajasree (Chuttimattathil), AB Beenu and Aparna Rajan represented Surya. Advocate Rinu S Aswan represented Mithran. items.title: Supreme Court orders halt on appointment of unqualified teachers to schools, colleges
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday passed an interim direction restraining the appointment or continuation of unqualified teachers in schools and colleges. A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana passed the order in a case concerning Assam's teacher provincialisation scheme. "As an interim measure, it is directed that no teacher shall be appointed/absorbed in schools or colleges unless such candidates possess the requisite prescribed qualification under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009/ The National Council for Teacher Education Act, 1993/ The University Grants Commission Act, 1956 till further orders," the Court said. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana CJI Kant remarked that continuing to induct unqualified persons as teachers would destroy the future of students. " Such kind of thing will destroy future generations." The Court passed the order while issuing notice on a public interest litigation (PIL) challenging the Assam Education (Provincialisation of Services of Teachers and Re-organisation of Educational Institutions) Act, 2017. Senior Advocate Ranjit Kumar , appearing for the petitioner, told the Court that Assam had appointed teachers in localities to keep schools running and that this scheme was later validated through a 2018 amendment to the 2017 Act. The validating amendment was under challenge before the Gauhati High Court in Mohor Ali Sheikh and Others v. State of Assam . A division bench of the High Court, in a judgment dated October 4, 2024, examined the constitutionality of the provincialisation framework and directed the State to put in place a regular pay scale for the affected tutors, commensurate with the schedule under the governing Act. Kumar told the Supreme Court that the High Court had also made observations concerning teachers found to be unqualified, directing that they continue to be paid their full salaries. items.title: Let him repent: Supreme Court on judge transferred to Naxalite area for losing temper, shouting at Bombay HC
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday sought the response of the Bombay High Court on a plea challenging contempt of court proceedings initiated against a senior judicial officer from Maharashtra over his alleged outburst before the High Court [ Dilip S Ghumare Versus High Court of Judicature at Bombay and Ors. ]. A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta however declined to stay the contempt proceedings against the officer, one Dilip S Ghumare, who was allegedly transferred to a naxalite area shortly after the Bombay High Court took exception to his actions. "Let him repent. This is gross indiscipline. A judicial officer cannot shout at the High Court" the Court said. items.title: Kerala HC orders Meta to block video containing derogatory remarks on Sabarimala deities
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Thursday directed Meta to temporarily block public access to a social media video containing scandalous and indecent remarks against Sabarimala deities [Rahul K Easwar v State of Kerala & ors]. Justice G Girish passed the interim order on a plea filed by right-wing activist and public commentator Rahul K Easwar who moved the Court seeking removal of the video and action against the Dalit activist Sunny M Kapikad who made the derogatory comments. After viewing the objectionable video, the Court observed that the continued availability of the video on social media could hurt the religious sentiments of devotees and passed an interim order restricting access to the video. " It appears that the allegation of the petitioner herein about the scandalous and indecent speech made by the respondent about the deities of Sabarimala temple is found to be substantiated. In continuance of the above video in the social media platform would definitely hurt the religious beliefs of the worshippers of the aforesaid deity. In the above circumstances, the 4th respondent (Meta Platforms) is hereby directed to temporarily block and disable public access to the above video at the URL (so and so), " the Court added. Further, the Court clarified that the interim direction was confined to that particular URL. The matter will be heard next on October 6. Justice G Girish Easwar sought directions to the state authorities to remove, block and disable public access to an objectionable video posted on social media in which Kapikad is alleged to have made the remarks against Sabarimala deities Lord Ayyappa and Malikappurathamma. items.summary: The Karnataka High Court has directed the Registrar (Judicial), Registrar General and Registrar (Computers) to implement e-notarisation in filings before the Karnataka high Court and the District Court. Justice Suraj Govindaraj directed the acceptance of e-notarisation while taking on record a compliance affidavit that was notarised electronically. The order was passed in a case relating to the restrictions imposed on a bank account pursuant to a cybercrime investigation. Justice Suraj Govindraj Counsel for IIFL Finance Limited, Advocate Priyanka S Bhat, provided a detailed process on how the e-notarisation was obtained in a memorandum of facts filed before the Court. The authorised signatory and notary joined a live audio-video conference with the same affidavit displayed on their screen. The notary verified the signatory's identity and authority to act for the company, confirmed understanding of what was being signed, recorded voluntary participation and administered an oath that the signatory had verified the contents of the affidavit. The signatory then electronically signed using Aadhaar-based e-KYC. The notary then stamped with her official seal and electronically signed the affidavit. items.title: ADR should not become a privilege for those who can afford it: Justice Sandeep Mehta
items.summary: Alternative dispute resolution (ADR) should not become a privilege available only to parties who can afford sophisticated dispute resolution mechanisms, Supreme Court Justice Sandeep Mehta said on Thursday. Justice Mehta said the success of ADR could not be measured merely by speed, efficiency or the number of institutions established. “ ADR should not become a privilege, available only to those who can afford the cost of sophisticated dispute resolution, ” he said. The judge was speaking at the Delhi chapter of India ADR Week 2026 , organised by the Mumbai Centre for International Arbitration (MCIA). Justice Mehta said cost and accessibility were equally important. If dispute resolution became excessively expensive, it could itself become a barrier of the kind ADR was intended to remove. He also referred to the move away from arbitration in some government contracts. The dispute resolution ecosystem, he said, must remain sophisticated without becoming unnecessarily expensive. Justice Mehta stressed that ADR was not synonymous with arbitration. Arbitration, mediation, conciliation, negotiation and Lok Adalats were different mechanisms suited to different disputes. He also warned against arbitral proceedings replicating the delays and procedural complexity of conventional litigation. “ If arbitral proceedings begin to duplicate the procedural complexity, the delays and the technicality of court proceedings, the very purpose of arbitration will be defeated ,” he said. The judge added that courts had an important but limited supervisory role. Judicial intervention should protect the integrity of arbitration while allowing proceedings to reach their conclusion without unnecessary interference. Justice Mehta also addressed artificial intelligence (AI). He said AI could assist tribunals with document review, case analysis and evidence management, but could not take over the adjudicatory function. “ AI may assist a tribunal, or as it does the court, in understanding it. It cannot assume responsibility for the judgment that follows ,” he said. Senior Advocate Nakul Dewan KC , delivered the vote of thanks. items.title: NCLT President has power to transfer cases across benches: NCLAT
items.summary: The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) on Wednesday held that the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) president has powers to transfer cases across benches in various territorial jurisdictions [Kamalesh v. Praveen] A three-member Bench of Judicial Member Justice Sharad Kumar Sharma and Technical Members Arun Baroka and Indevar Pandey held that the NCLT president can transfer proceedings from one bench to another where the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) requires such a transfer. “ The power of president NCLT is not restricted nor clouded to any territorial location ,” the appellate tribunal said. The NCLAT was dealing with insolvency proceedings against Kamlesh Rani Singla, a suspended director and personal guarantor of Laxmi Pipes Limited. The corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP) of Laxmi Pipes was already pending before NCLT Chandigarh. However, proceedings under Section 95 of the IBC against Singla were initiated before NCLT in New Delhi. Singla sought transfer of the personal guarantor proceedings to Chandigarh. The NCLT president rejected her transfer plea in December 2025. The decision relied on an October 2025 judgment of the Gujarat High Court in Arcelor Mittal Nippon Steel India Limited v. National Company Law Tribunal & Ors. The High Court had held that Rule 16(d) of the NCLT Rules did not empower the NCLT president to transfer a case beyond the territorial jurisdiction of a particular bench. It said that the president’s authority was confined to benches falling within the same territorial limits. This decision is currently under challenge before the Supreme Court. The NCLAT disagreed with this interpretation of the High Court. It held that Rule 16(d), read with Section 60(2) of the IBC and Rule 2(7) of the NCLT Rules, gives the president sufficient power to transfer a case from one bench to another. The Appellate Tribunal said that restricting that power to the same territorial jurisdiction could create “anomalous situations”. The NCLAT also stressed that Section 60(2) of the IBC requires insolvency proceedings against a personal guarantor to be filed before the same NCLT where the CIRP or liquidation of the corporate debtor is pending. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday set aside the compulsory retirement of an Indian Trade Service officer who was treated as “deadwood” barely two-and-a-half months after his promotion to the Joint Secretary level. [SS Das v. Union of India] In a judgment delivered on September 9, a Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu directed the Centre to pay former officer SS Das ₹9 lakh as compensation for the loss of his reputation and ₹6 lakh as costs. Since Das has already reached the age of superannuation, the Court directed the Director General of Foreign Trade to call him back to office and accord him a farewell with full honour, as he would have received upon his regular retirement. The Court held that the decisions to promote Das and then almost immediately treat him as “deadwood” were mutually contradictory. “ Having promoted the appellant, barely a couple of months later, the superior officers in the department could not have branded him, so to say, ‘dead wood’ to justify weeding him out in purported public interest. The two actions are mutually destructive and cannot co-exist, ” it said. Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu Das joined the Indian Trade Service in 1989 and received several promotions during his career. He was placed in the Senior Administrative Grade at the Joint Secretary level in November 2017 and regularly promoted to the grade on February 27, 2018. However, on May 10, 2018, the Centre compulsorily retired him under Fundamental Rule 56(j), a little less than 5 years before his superannuation. The decision was based on entries in his service record and a confidential note alleging that his handling of an anti-dumping investigation was unprofessional. The note also recorded an oral allegation by industry representatives that Das had demanded certain favours. However, there was neither a written complaint nor any evidence supporting the allegation. Das challenged the decision before the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT), which dismissed his plea in July 2021. The Delhi High Court upheld the CAT’s decision in January 2024, prompting Das to approach the Supreme Court. After examining his service records, the Supreme Court found that Das had consistently received “outstanding” or “very good” assessments. items.title: Vinesh Phogat case: Delhi HC says WFI must balance interests of nation and women athletes returning after childbirth
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday remarked that the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) must come up with guidelines to enable participation of female athletes returning after maternity leave. Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma said that a balance must be struck between the interests of the country and the athlete. The Court made the remark while hearing Olympian Vinesh Phogat’s plea seeking directions to allow her to participate in the trials for the Senior World Wrestling Championship scheduled on September 14. Senior Advocate Rajshekhar Rao appeared for Phogat and told the Bench that the WFI has displayed “absolute arbitrariness” in the case and she was informed of the selection criteria only on September 7. “Effectively, it means I am out of reckoning for two more years and I am finished as an athlete,” he said. The counsel appearing for the WFI told the Bench that Phogat has not been banned from participation. He said that the medal winners from 2025 and 2026 are eligible for selection for this year’s World Championship and Phogat can participate at the state and national levels and make her way up. However, Justice Sharma said that such a policy is a "problem". “This is the problem. A woman, she will get married, she will give birth to a child and in that interim period, men will go and win medals and then they will qualify and someone will have to sit back at home and look after the children. There should be something that you have to do about this also, otherwise this is being very unfair," the Court said. It said that the situation in the legal profession was no different. "In this profession [law] also, when one is practising law, when they have children and when they come back, the clients do not come. This is something that we are trying to address because you have failed to. How unfair can this can be? Therefore, you have to make some guidelines which will balance the interest of the country also and the person also,” the Bench said. Justice Sharma added that she had been a judge for 35 years and things have changed very little. Ultimately, the judge said that she will decide Phogat’s plea and pass an order. The Court was hearing the two fresh applications moved by Phogat in her already pending petitions before the High Court. items.title: Solomon Pappaiah, Tamil scholar and celebrated Pattimandram moderator, dies at 90
items.summary: Renowned Tamil scholar and veteran Pattimandram moderator Solomon Pappaiah died at a private hospital in Madurai on Friday, September 11, following age-related health complications. He was 90. Pappaiah had been undergoing treatment for several days after his health deteriorated, with his family confirming his death at the hospital. For several generations of Tamil television viewers, Pappaiah was a familiar face associated with Pattimandram, the traditional Tamil debate format in which speakers argue opposing sides of a literary, social or cultural topic. As a moderator, he helped take the format beyond academic and literary circles and into homes across Tamil Nadu and among Tamil-speaking audiences elsewhere. Pappaiah was a former Tamil professor at The American College in Madurai and became one of Tamil Nadu’s best-known debate moderators, taking literary and social discussions to a wider television audience. His ability to combine humour with serious literary and social commentary made him particularly popular with television audiences. Born on February 22, 1936, his birth name was Sundaram Solomon Pappaiah. After his academic career, he became widely recognised through televised Pattimandrams, where his contribution went beyond simply moderating debates. He conducted more than 12,000 Pattimandrams during his lifetime. His speeches during Pattimandrams often connected classical Tamil literature with everyday life. He introduced audiences to subjects ranging from Bharathiyar’s poetry to Kambar’s epic works, explaining them in a manner that was both scholarly and easy to understand. His humorous and conversational style became a defining feature of his public appearances. He was also an expert on Tamil literary works. He wrote commentaries on the Thirukkural and other works of Tamil literature. His career as a writer, speaker and academic complemented his work as a Pattimandram moderator, establishing him as a prominent public figure in Tamil literary and cultural circles. Pappaiah was recognised with the Tamil Nadu government’s Kalaimamani award in 2000 for his contribution to Tamil language and literature. In 2021, he received the Padma Shri for his contribution to literature and education. Pappaiah was the first Pattimandram moderator to receive the Padma Shri. items.summary: A 29-year-old woman confessed to killing her one-year-old daughter at Vilavoorkal in Thiruvananthapuram on Thursday, September 10. The woman, who consumed medicines in a suspected suicide attempt, is in observation at the Government Medical College under police custody. As per the first information report, the woman, Christy Thomas, made grievous injuries to her daughter Evana alias Anna using a knife. The incident happened between 3.30 and 4.30 pm in their bedroom. When relatives learnt about the incident, they rushed the child to a nearby primary health centre and later to SAT Hospital. However, Evana was declared dead by the evening. The knife used for the murder was recovered from the bedroom. Christy has been charged under section 103 (1) (murder) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Police said that Christy confessed to the crime but did not give any reason for murdering her lone child. The incident happened on the fourth wedding anniversary of Christy and her husband, Abhijith. As per reports, the couple had been facing marital discord for a while. Police have not recorded Christy’s arrest as she is under medical observation following her suicide attempt. Evana’s body will be handed over to relatives after a post-mortem examination on Friday. Christy will be produced in court after completion of her observation period. ‘Psychiatric evaluation needed’ While the police said there was no clarity on whether Christy was experiencing any mental health issues, mental health experts said a psychiatric evaluation was necessary in cases like this. “Mental health assessments should normally be conducted during the perinatal period to identify conditions such as postpartum blues, depression or psychosis. The police often do not mention whether an accused person was experiencing mental health issues because of the perception that a diagnosis could result in the accused being released. That should not be the case. items.title: Bengaluru pothole leaves woman needing plastic surgery
items.summary: A water-filled pothole turned Bengaluru resident Aishani Khanna’s routine commute into a serious accident. Her scooter fell, crushing her ankle and leaving her with deep cuts, severe skin damage and significant blood loss. She also underwent plastic surgery and paid nearly ₹2 lakh for treatment. Aishani’s accident is not an isolated case. Data tabled in Parliament shows Bengaluru recorded 93 pothole-related accidents and 24 deaths in 2024. NCRB data has also recorded the city as having the highest number of deaths due to civic negligence for six consecutive years.

items.title: Renukaswamy case: Karnataka HC weighs options for Darshan’s physical presence at trial
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court, on Thursday, September 10 suggested alternatives to the regular physical production of Kannada actor Darshan Thoogudeepa before the trial court in the Renukaswamy murder case, noting that producing him in court on every date could pose security and traffic concerns. Justice V Srishananda was hearing a petition filed by Darshan’s wife, Vijayalakshmi, seeking permission for the actor, who is the second accused in the case, to be physically produced before the trial court for the duration of the trial instead of appearing through video conference from Bengaluru Central Prison. She had appealed the high court after a trial court rejected her petition stating that recurring technical and connectivity problems during video-conferencing proceedings prevented Darshan from effectively following the trial. The court observed that Darshan could instead be physically produced when key witnesses are examined and cross-examined. It also suggested that the trial could potentially be shifted to the special court at Parappana Agrahara, where an exclusive facility is available for conducting proceedings involving prisoners. The court asked Special Public Prosecutor P Prasanna Kumar and senior advocate Hashmath Pasha, who represents Darshan, to submit the modalities for examining and cross-examining the important witnesses. The High Court also suggested that the examination of material witnesses could be completed within a few days. Darshan could be physically produced before the trial court for three or four days to facilitate the examination and cross-examination of these witnesses, the court said. Another option suggested by the court was to allow Darshan’s lawyers to have a private and confidential conversation with him before each hearing. Justice Srishananda said the trial court’s official video-conferencing infrastructure, including a mobile phone with video-calling and headphone facilities, could be used to facilitate such consultations. SPP Prasanna Kumar told the court that he had already suggested before the trial court that Darshan could be physically produced for a few days during the examination and cross-examination of important witnesses. items.title: Tamil Nadu: Sanitation worker, rescuer die after inhaling toxic gas during manual scavenging
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A sanitation worker engaged in manual scavenging and a man who attempted to rescue him died after allegedly inhaling toxic gas while manually cleaning a septic tank at a house near Kallakudi in Tamil Nadu’s Tiruchirappalli district on September 2. The deceased have been identified as Ganesh (25) from Kumbakonam, and Mukesh Kumar (26), a native of Bihar who was residing at the house where the incident occurred. According to the police, Ganesh, who was employed by Sahana Septic Tank Cleaning, entered the septic tank without adequate protective equipment to clean it. He reportedly lost consciousness after inhaling toxic gas inside the tank. Seeing Ganesh collapse, Mukesh Kumar attempted to rescue him by entering the tank. He too became unconscious after being exposed to the gas. Both men died after inhaling the toxic gas, police said. Speaking to TNM, Kallakudi police said that the postmortem reports are awaited and that an investigation into the incident is underway. Similar incidents have been reported in the past. In Idukki, three men died after entering a drain to rescue a worker who had collapsed while cleaning it. Jayaram, who had entered the drain first, became unconscious, following which Sundarapandian and Michael entered in an attempt to rescue him. All three died. In Chennai, three members of the same family, along with three others who attempted to rescue them, died after allegedly inhaling toxic gas from a septic tank. The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013 prohibits the employment of people as manual scavengers and provides for their rehabilitation. The section defines “manual scavenger” as a person who manually cleans, carries, disposes of, or handles human excreta in any manner in an insanitary latrine or in an open drain or a pit into which the human excreta from the insanitary latrines is disposed of, or on a railway track or other such spaces or premises. This does not include a sewer or a septic tank. The Act separately defines “hazardous cleaning” of a sewer or septic tank as “manual cleaning” by a worker without the employer providing them with protective gear, other cleaning devices, and without following safety precautions. This narrow and ambiguous definition is utilised by employers to hire workers to do manual scavenging. This story was written by a student interning with TNM.

items.title: 3 killed, 14 injured as roof of under-construction church collapses in Vellore
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Three people died, and 14 were injured after a slab from an under-construction church collapsed in Vellore’s Manjukrishnapuram on Thursday, September 10. The roof of the CSI Zion Hill Church, where concreting works were underway, collapsed, trapping several workers under the debris. The deceased were identified as John, a 39-year-old building contractor from Bengaluru, and Emmanuel (45) and Samuel (45), two daily wage labourers from Andhra Pradesh. The police said that four workers who suffered severe injuries were admitted to the Government Medical College Hospital in Adukkamparai and the Christian Medical College (CMC) Hospital in Vellore. Ten others who were trapped under the debris were rescued and are being treated for minor injuries. The Thiruvalam police and Katpadi Fire Rescue services, along with a team of 30 from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and four sniffer dogs from the Arokkam unit, conducted the search and rescue operations. They were also assisted by the police and other officials from Andhra Pradesh. Vellore district collector PS Leela Alex, Ranipet Superintendent of Police P Sibin and Katpadi MLA Dr M Sudhakar inspected the site. The collector announced an investigation into the incident, promising a thorough review of the approvals and permits related to the construction. The Thiruvalam Police said that the postmortem of the deceased is ongoing and further investigation is underway. The district administration has also started raising financial relief for the victims and their families, officials said. This story was written by a student interning with TNM.

items.title: From biological weapons to espionage: What Anthropic’s report reveals about AI misuse
items.summary: Artificial intelligence is increasingly being used not just to help people carry out malicious activities, but to take over several steps of those operations, according to a new report by AI company Anthropic. The company said it identified and disrupted attempts to use its Claude AI models for cyberattacks, espionage, surveillance, scams, influence operations, conventional weapons development and research that could potentially support biological weapons development between December 2025 and August 2026. The cases ranged from a Russia-linked cyber espionage campaign and an automated fake-news operation in Bangladesh to systems designed to identify dissidents and attempts to use Claude in research involving viruses and toxins. Anthropic said the actors involved included suspected state-sponsored groups, criminals, commercial spyware companies, propaganda organisations and politically motivated individuals. The findings are detailed in Anthropic's 154-page report, Detecting and Countering Misuse of AI: September 2026 , the company's fourth threat intelligence report. Anthropic said it was publishing the findings because it had a “responsibility to disclose malicious misuse” of its services. The company said its Claude Haiku, Sonnet and Opus models were used in the cases examined. None of the cases involved Claude Fable or its Mythos-class models, except for one case involving attempts to copy the capabilities of its AI through a process known as distillation. Across the cases, Anthropic said it has seen a change in the way AI is being misused. The concern is no longer simply that someone can ask an AI chatbot to write malicious code or provide instructions. Increasingly, AI can be connected to other software and used to carry out several parts of an operation. AI is doing more of the work One of the biggest findings of the report is that AI is increasingly being used to do more than provide information or write computer code. Anthropic said attackers are using AI to handle several parts of an operation — from finding potential targets and looking for weaknesses to stealing and processing information. In some cases, several AI systems were used to work on different tasks at the same time, with humans setting the broad objectives and checking the results. This could make sophisticated attacks possible with fewer people and less technical expertise than would traditionally have been required, Anthropic said.
